notes: One typescript sheet with handwritten own pagination '- 4 -' at the top and archive number 68 at the lower left. There is one heading, 'Commentaires Appendice', no date, no signature, no letterhead and no stamp. The page has fifteen body paragraphs: the preliminary p.37 correction and fourteen appendix comments, counting the separate Donner aussi paragraph. The handwritten interventions in the p.5 item are three quotation pairs and a rightward double arrow. Their author cannot be established from this isolated sheet, so the inventory says unnamed hand. The two isolated graphic observations are also left without asserted authorship; they could be incidental marks. There are no drawn mathematical diagrams or separate mathematical displays: the text asks for a diagram but does not draw one. The page explicitly asks whether to detail the proof of 7.4, which K with raised point is intended in 7.1, for a reference to the regularity implication, to see the p.6 argument, for references to Gr_top and filtration compatibility, whether connexe should be added to two terms, and for a reference containing the last assertion's proof. These are the author's requests and doubts, not completed proof checks. All five explicit C doubts were inspected on one tight crop each; the quotation orientation and isolated spot remain unresolved, while the a underprint, underlined Q and final d underprint have decisions. The crop for Q also revealed the detached lower-left pair, which is retained graphically with uncertain status. The final supposed accent is an ascender and foot of a typewritten d overwritten by e. The preliminary spellings composé/composée, the opposed récrire/réécrire, and standard/standart were read independently and retained. H supplies description only; it is unavailable for transcription collation, all h_reading fields are null and all diff_h fields are false. Its assertion about absence of handwriting was not used as an authority. The cotefile wrapper in C is omitted by the current per-page convention; this is metadata handling, not a manuscript difference. The last-line question mark follows question without an intervening typed space. Line-end hyphenations in relative, algébrique and intention are joined under the supplied conventions.
math_reading_decisions: K has a separate filled raised point. It is transcribed K^{\bullet}; there is no visible prime, star or index. No claim about the intended complex has been supplied.

The first X has lowered t, the second lowered s, and the consequent X is unindexed. The pen sign has two horizontal shafts and a rightward head, so it is \Rightarrow. Regularity is the statement quoted by the page, not a result independently checked here.
The letters Y, S, K and the X letters are ordinary single-struck typewritten capitals. Their printed weight has not been converted to bold or double-struck alphabets.
The p.7 clause contains X = S and an underlined Z. The separate low rule under Z is retained as \underline{Z}; no double-struck diagonal is supplied.

The first Gr expression has a raised filled point and the lowered roman letters top. The second has a raised filled point, an empty pair of parentheses and a lowered Q with a separate underline. The single oval plus tail and low rule settle \underline{Q}; the expected coefficient field was not used to select its alphabet.
The lower-case g after pour is the printed letter g. The adjective sequence projectif, d’intersection complète, et de dimension relative virtuelle donnée is retained without mathematical correction.
The two detached marks under the later r are reproduced geometrically and are not made into a mathematical subscript, punctuation mark or assertion.

The requests for proofs, references and a diagram were read for symbol identity and placement only. No proof, computation, external comparison or mathematical background result was used as a verification event.
